equity_bridge.item: Redeemable non-controlling interests at carrying value (30 June 2026)
equity_bridge.note: Q2 2026 balance sheet, note 11; put/call minority stakes in subsidiaries. Flows are modelled at 100%, so this is the single NCI charge.
Q2 2026 balance sheet, note 10: 24.121 + 9.576. Deferred purchase price on completed acquisitions, debt-like.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: management's mid-single-digit organic guidance plus a ~3pp tuck-in M&A contribution at the FY2024-25 spend-to-growth relationship, charged in capex. The equity CAGR (house default) is rejected as a source: it is inflated by ~$60M/yr of option-exercise proceeds and by acquisition-funded growth that this model charges for separately.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 15.8% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 9.4% (and owner-FCF 5yr CAGR 3.9%) -- divergence >30%. Book value compounds on acquisitions and option proceeds; per-share earnings and owner cash flow have grown far slower. Equity CAGR is not used.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs run FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr). FY2019 is excluded as a start point: GAAP EPS of -$6.58 that year is the ~$314M LTIA settlement, not earnings power. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC: FY2020 240.7 -> FY2025 290.8 (3.9%/yr) versus reported FCF 252.4 -> 318.2 (4.7%/yr); SBC grew 18.7%/yr over the same period, so a growing (if still small) share of reported FCF growth is being paid in stock. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is left null because the FY2022 base (10.2) was a working-capital trough and the arithmetic (~200%/yr) is meaningless. Revenue grew ~14%/yr but FY2024's +20% included the Roofing Corp platform deal; FY2025's +5% was 100% acquisitions with organic flat to negative.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 at ~4% total growth with Brands organic still negative, a weather/housing normalisation spread over FY2027-28 taking growth to ~7% (3pp of it bought via tuck-ins charged at 2.5% of revenue), slow margin expansion to 11.3%, deceleration to 3% terminal growth as the M&A allowance tapers to 1%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Organic rebound in restoration/roofing and housing-linked brands plus the tuck-in machine at full pace delivers ~9-10% growth for several years and a 12% EBITDA margin; this is the roll-up compounding story the current multiple is paying for.
scenario_narratives.bear: Prolonged housing/weather downturn keeps Brands organic negative, margins slip to 9.6%, a goodwill impairment lands, M&A slows, and FirstService becomes a 3-4% grower capitalised at 15x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: FirstService is valued as an operating roll-up on owner free cash flow: EBITDA after stock-based compensation, cash taxes, PP&E capex AND a tuck-in acquisition allowance, with the growth those acquisitions buy credited in the revenue path and tapered together with the spend. Reported FCF ignores the ~$100-200M/yr of acquisition spend that produces most of the reported growth, so this model's year-1 owner-FCF margin (~3%) is well below the reported-basis 5.3%. The minority (RNCI) claim and deferred purchase price are deducted once in the bridge; operating leases are left inside EBITDA under US GAAP; a single 8.5% USD WACC is used across scenarios with risk carried in the flows and weights. Values are computed in USD and converted to CAD at 1.4253 for the TSX quote. At the current price the market is paying for the bull-case roll-up compounding (multiple arbitrage on tuck-ins bought at ~8-9x EBITDA inside a ~13x EV/EBITDA parent); the house base case does not grant that arbitrage.
key_risks_to_valuation: M&A treatment is the largest judgment: charging 2.5% of revenue for tuck-ins while crediting ~3pp of growth assumes acquisitions roughly earn the WACC; if FirstService's deals are durably accretive well above WACC (the bull thesis) the base understates value, and if integration falters it overstates it.
Brands organic revenue is weather- and housing-dependent; a multi-year continuation of the FY2025-26 decline moves the outcome toward the bear case and risks a goodwill impairment.
RNCI deducted at carrying value (US$507M) rather than the lower formula redemption amount (~US$417M at YE2025); using the formula amount would add ~US$2/share.
USD/CAD: a 5% move in the rate moves the CAD intrinsic value by 5% with no change in the business; the fx_rate is dated 2026-10-10 and must be refreshed with the price.
Terminal value is capped at 18x owner FCF (15x bear); the Gordon value at 8.5%/3% would be ~18.7x, so the cap binds slightly in base and bull.
Cash tax held at 28%; a shift of deal structures toward asset purchases (deductible Section 197 amortisation) would lower it and add value.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, TSX quote in CAD, at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 169.60-266.83. Nasdaq FSV (USD) used only for the FX parity check in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.fx: Yahoo Finance CADUSD=X, 2026-10-10, inverted to USD->CAD.
data_sources.financials: FSV.TO_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized (USD millions, FY2014-FY2025 annual, quarterly to Q2 2026); FY2025 audited statements (FSV.TO_Financials_FY2025.txt: balance sheet 240-272, cash flow 307-351, RNCI note 983-1011, taxes paid 1163-1171, diluted shares 1196-1210); Q2 2026 unaudited statements (FSV.TO_Quarterly_Q2-2026_FinancialStatements.txt: balance sheet 143-186, shareholders' equity 204-225, EPS note 630-638); FY2025 MD&A for guidance, interest rate and RNCI commentary.
data_sources.qualitative: FSV.TO_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): segment mix, bull/bear axes, FY2026 guidance, Q2 2026 call commentary.

inputs.share_count_basis: 44,154,011 Common Shares issued and outstanding at 30 June 2026 (Q2 2026 statement of shareholders' equity, after 1,827,750 shares purchased for cancellation in Q2) plus ~6k treasury-method option dilution; the Q2 2026 EPS note shows only 1k dilutive option shares at the quarter's average price, so the options are essentially out of the money. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The ~2.7M shares that could settle RNCI puts are NOT added here because the RNCI claim is deducted at value in the equity bridge (charge once).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Stock-based compensation' add-back $27,387k (FSV.TO_Financials_FY2025.txt:318); equity-award taxes are nil because the plan is a cash-exercise stock option plan (options exercised for $62.0M cash proceeds, no net-share settlement). Adjusted EBITDA as the company defines it excludes SBC, so the engine's SBC deduction from the EBITDA margin path is the right basis.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY2025 repurchases were nil. In Q2 2026 the company bought back 1,827,750 shares for $248.4M (~US$135.91/share) under the NCIB; that is already reflected in the 44.16M count used here. The flat count is therefore funded, not a modelling convention: SBC of ~$27M/yr is tiny against FCF and the company is a net repurchaser as of H1 2026.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in USD (MJDS filer, US GAAP). Price is the TSX quote in CAD. fx_rate is USD->CAD = 1/0.7016 = 1.4253, Yahoo CADUSD=X at 2026-10-10. Parity check against the Nasdaq dual listing (FSV, USD): TSX C$185.09 x 0.7016 = US$129.86 vs Nasdaq close US$129.73 on 2026-10-09, a 0.1% tie that confirms the rate, the direction and the quote basis. Per-share values are computed in USD and converted to CAD; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are CAD so they compare directly to current_price.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close, TSX (Friday; 10 Oct is a Saturday, so this is the latest regular close, not an after-hours print)
inputs.net_debt_note: Long-term debt current 13.636 + non-current 1,236.731 = 1,250.367 (Q2 2026 balance sheet, note 9; borrowings only, finance leases on vehicles are immaterial and already inside long-term debt). Cash 173.351 excludes restricted cash of 27.787 (customer trust / insurance collateral, operating). Net debt rose from 928.3 at YE2025 to 1,077.0 mainly because the $248M Q2 2026 buyback was revolver-funded. Operating lease liabilities (59.978 + 248.953 = 308.9) are deliberately excluded -- see lease_treatment.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows. Risk-free 10y UST ~4.2%; ERP 5.0%; beta ~1.0 for a diversified North American services roll-up gives a cost of equity of ~9.2%, plus ~0.3pp for a mid-cap with roll-up execution risk = 9.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt 6.3% (FY2025 weighted average on the revolver, Financials FY2025 line 944), 4.5% after tax at 28%. Capital structure at market: equity ~US$5.7B vs debt + RNCI + contingent consideration ~US$1.6B, roughly 80/20. WACC = 0.80 x 9.5 + 0.20 x 4.5 = 8.5%. The same 8.5% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, weather and housing risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP (ASC 842). Operating lease cost ($68.7M cash paid in FY2025, Financials line 792) is a straight-line operating expense inside the company's Adjusted EBITDA, so it is already deducted from the ebitda_margin_path; right-of-use amortisation is NOT in the D&A line. Lease liabilities ($308.9M at 30 June 2026) are therefore excluded from net debt. This is treatment (B) with no extra lease_cost_pct_path needed -- adding one, or adding the liabilities to net debt, would charge the leases twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled at 100% consolidated and the redeemable non-controlling interests (RNCI) are deducted once in the equity bridge at the 30 June 2026 carrying value of US$507.4M. RNCI are put/call minority stakes held by subsidiary managers, carried at the greater of the formula redemption amount (fixed multiple of trailing EBITDA; $416.8M at YE2025) and the initially recorded amount. The carrying value is the conservative choice: it is what the balance sheet says the claim is worth, and it sits close to the value-share implied by the RNCI's ~8% share of total net earnings (15.9 of 190.7 in FY2025) applied to the modelled equity value. Calibration: FY2025 unlevered NOPAT at 28% ties to total net earnings of 190.7 after after-tax interest within ~$10M of acquisition-related noise, so no leakage driver is needed in the flows. Contingent acquisition consideration (24.1 current + 9.6 non-current = 33.7) is deferred purchase price on completed deals and is deducted as debt-like.
inputs.ma_treatment: FirstService is a serial tuck-in acquirer (9 deals for $107.2M in FY2025; FY2021-25 average ex the $413M Roofing Corp platform deal ~$134M/yr, ~2.5-3% of revenue) and management's 10%+ growth algorithm is roughly half M&A. Reported FCF (OCF - PP&E capex) excludes that spend entirely, so a DCF that credits acquired growth without charging for it overstates value. Choice: the capex_pct_path is PP&E capex (2.3% of revenue, FY2025 actual 2.32%) PLUS a tuck-in M&A allowance, 2.5% of revenue in the base case (bull 3.0%, bear 1.5%), tapering with the growth path so that by year 10 the allowance (1.0% base) is consistent with the ~0.5-1pp of acquired growth still assumed; the terminal year does not pay for growth it no longer receives. The growth path credits ~3pp/yr (base) from tuck-ins in years 2-6 at ~0.85x revenue purchase prices, the observed FY2024-25 relationship ($319M of spend bought ~5pp of FY2025 growth). Platform acquisitions like Roofing Corp are excluded from both the spend and the growth and must be judged on their own terms when they occur. At ~8-9x EBITDA purchase multiples the acquired FCF yield plus organic growth roughly earns the 8.5% WACC, so the valuation is not very sensitive to the M&A pace as long as spend and growth move together; what the market is paying for above this model is the roll-up multiple arbitrage, which is stated as the bull axis rather than baked into the base.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, three-scenario probability-weighted, built through the Drivers/engine route (owner_fcf_dcf_component). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md as an operating company (residential HOA management + franchised/company-owned property-service brands); not a REIT, bank or holdco. Non-US adaptations applied: dual currency (USD flows, CAD quote, fx_rate 1.4253 with Nasdaq parity check), US GAAP leases inside EBITDA, RNCI deducted once in the bridge, risk charged once (single WACC). FY0 is FY2025 (Dec year-end); the latest filing is Q2 2026 (30 June 2026) and supplies net debt, cash, RNCI and the share count. Owner FCF FY2025 = 318.236 reported FCF (OCF 445.941 - PP&E 127.705) - 27.387 SBC - 0 interest income = 290.849. Interest income is nil in the filings and the company is a net borrower, so there is no cash-pile double count. FY2025 OCF was flattered by a ~$54M working-capital inflow (receivables collection), so the component build, not the FY2025 margin, drives year 1: the modelled FY2026 owner-FCF margin after the tuck-in allowance is ~3%, versus the 5.3% reported-basis FY2025 owner margin. FY2019 one-off: GAAP net earnings of -$251.6M and EPS of -$6.58 reflect the ~$314M cash settlement of the Long-Term Incentive Arrangement with the Founder/Chairman; it is not an impairment and not a trough earnings input -- the FY0 anchor is FY2025 and the LTIA only matters in that the EPS and equity CAGRs below are computed from FY2020 onward to avoid it. Brands organic revenue has been negative for several quarters (-3% FY2025, -7% Q4 2025, -3% Q2 2026) on soft housing, weak consumer confidence and mild weather; H1 2026 consolidated growth was +3.7% and management guided H2 similar or modestly better, so year-1 growth is 4.0% in the base (below the 10%+ algorithm) with the recovery toward 7% spread over years 2-4 rather than assumed immediately. Cash tax at 28%: FY2025 income taxes paid were $82.4M against 27% statutory, the excess reflecting partly non-deductible acquired-intangible amortisation. Working-capital capture is -4% of the revenue change: receivables (~16% of revenue) and inventories exceed payables plus unearned revenue, so growth consumes cash (FY2024: -$40M on +$882M revenue). SBC projected at 0.5% of revenue flat (FY2025 actual 0.50%); band_position is reported because SBC is non-zero, but the house/street spread is small for this company.

bear.capex_note: PP&E 2.3% + tuck-in M&A allowance 1.5% tapering to 0.5% as deal pace slows with the Brands downturn
bear.narrative: The Brands organic decline persists: housing stays frozen by higher-for-longer rates, consumer confidence weak, restoration claims subdued, and the Brands reporting unit whose fair value exceeded carrying value by <5% at YE2025 is impaired. Margins compress to 9.6% on labour and insurance inflation against flat revenue, the tuck-in pace halves, and the business settles into a 3-4% grower with a 15x terminal cap. Same 8.5% WACC -- the risk is in the flows, not the rate.

base.capex_note: PP&E 2.3% + tuck-in M&A allowance 2.5% tapering to 1.0% by year 10 in step with the growth deceleration
base.narrative: FY2026 grows ~4% (H1 +3.7%, H2 guided similar or modestly better) as Brands organic stays negative; weather-driven restoration/roofing demand normalises through FY2027-28 and Residential keeps 4-5% organic, lifting total growth to ~7% with ~3pp from tuck-ins charged at 2.5% of revenue. EBITDA margin extends its three-year expansion slowly from 10.2% to 11.3% (Residential process/AI gains, Brands operating leverage on recovery), then growth decelerates to 4% by year 10 and 3% terminal with the M&A allowance tapering alongside it.

bull.capex_note: PP&E 2.3% + tuck-in M&A allowance 3.0% tapering to 1.5%
bull.narrative: Management's 10%+ algorithm is nearly delivered: a sharp organic rebound in restoration/roofing as claims activity normalises, housing turnover recovers lifting California Closets/CertaPro/Floor Coverings, Roofing Corp's OneRoof integration and First Onsite's platform spend convert into margin, and the tuck-in machine runs at 3% of revenue buying ~4-5pp of growth. EBITDA margin reaches 12% by year 8.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because 58% of revenue (Brands) has posted negative organic growth for four-plus quarters with management guiding no inflection in H2 2026, and one Brands reporting unit sits within 5% of impairment -- that is a live, evidenced downside, not a hypothetical. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: weather-claims normalisation, a housing recovery, Roofing Corp integration paying off and the M&A pace holding. No going-concern or covenant risk (Debt/EBITDA ~2.0x after the buyback, $1.75B facility to 2030), so bear is not pushed beyond 25%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
